name: Caffeine
what_is: Caffeine is a stimulant found naturally in coffee, tea, cocoa and some other plants, and it can also be added directly to foods, drinks and supplements.
why_botia: Caffeine does not give you energy: it blocks the signal your body uses to tell you it is tired. The tiredness is still there, but you feel it less — and caffeine can disturb sleep even when taken six hours before bedtime. It can raise blood pressure for a few hours, particularly in people who do not consume it regularly. EFSA considers up to 400 mg per day not to raise safety concerns for healthy adults, and sets 200 mg per day during pregnancy; the ingredient list tells you caffeine is there, not necessarily how much.
can_1: Detect caffeine and common explicit ingredient names such as caffeine anhydrous when they appear in the ingredient list.
can_2: Explain how caffeine changes the feeling of tiredness, its effects on sleep and blood pressure, and the different EFSA intake level during pregnancy.
cannot_1: Calculate total caffeine from the ingredient list when the amount is not declared there.
cannot_2: Infer the exact caffeine dose from coffee, tea, guarana, cocoa or another caffeine-containing ingredient.

title: Caffeine
description: Caffeine does not remove tiredness: it blocks the signal that makes you feel it. It can disturb sleep, temporarily raise blood pressure and has a lower EFSA intake level during pregnancy.
